claim: The note says いい was taught in Lesson 9, but in my cards it came in Lesson 10.
evidence: Back note: 'A politeness step up from いい (ii, "Nice, good") from Lesson 9.' Ledger: いい | Good, nice is under Lesson 10: Describing Things; Lesson 9 has no card for いい.

claim: The note calls Lesson 16's ちょっと 'casual', but I learned that ちょっと as a polite way to decline, and the note never mentions the 'a little bit' meaning I already know, which is the one that applies here.
evidence: Back note: 'It is more formal than the casual ちょっと (chotto) "Well, it's a bit..." from Lesson 16, which here means "a moment", not a polite refusal.' Ledger: Lesson 16 ちょっと | Well, it's a bit... (used to decline politely); Lesson 10 ちょっと | A little bit.
fix: Rewrite the note to say that ちょっと here is Lesson 10's 'a little bit' (a moment), not Lesson 16's polite decline, and drop 'casual'.

claim: The Production front 'After' also fits the あとで card, whose English is 'Afterwards, after', so I cannot tell whether to say あと or あとで.
evidence: ato Production FRONT: 'Time / After' -> あと. ato-de Production FRONT: 'Time / Afterwards, after' -> あとで. Both fronts carry 'after' in the same category with no hint.
fix: Give the two cards English that do not overlap (for example 'After (X の あと)' and 'Afterwards, later'), or add a hint saying whether で is wanted.

claim: 'Have a meeting' is also how I would say かいぎがあります, since Lesson 14 taught あります as 'Have' and gave me 'Smith-san has a meeting tomorrow'.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Work & Occupations / Have a meeting' -> かいぎをします. Ledger: あります | Have; スミスさんはあしたかいぎがあります | Smith-san has a meeting tomorrow.
fix: Add a hint such as 'hold one, with します' or a note contrasting かいぎをします with かいぎがあります.

claim: The note talks about 'the one cell the book stars as an exception', which refers to a table in the textbook that I have never seen.
evidence: Back note: 'Regular 1, and the one cell the book stars as an exception. き (ki) normally gives いて (ite)...'
fix: Drop the reference to the book's table and just say いきます is the one exception to the き -> いて rule.

claim: Nothing on the front tells me to use the polite よろしい, so I answer いまいいですか, which I can build from cards I know and which fits the English just as well.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Greetings / Is now a good time?' with no scene. Answer: いまよろしいですか. The base card chotto-yoroshii-desu-ka has the scene 'to a busy boss or someone senior', this one has none. Ledger: いい | Good, nice; いいんですか | Are you sure?
fix: Add a scene like 'to your boss, politely' to the front.

claim: Nothing on the front asks for the polite よろしい, so あしたはいいですか answers it equally well.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Greetings / Is tomorrow all right?' with no scene. Answer: あしたはよろしいですか.
fix: Add a scene that sets a polite register (speaking to a client or a superior).

claim: Nothing on the front asks for the polite よろしい, so ここでいいですか (or ここはいいですか) fits the English just as well.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Grammar & Function Words / Is here all right?' with no scene. Answer: ここでよろしいですか.
fix: Add a scene that sets a polite register, such as a shop clerk asking a customer.

claim: The answer puts で after ここ, but no card taught 'X で いいです / よろしいです', and the sister cards use は (あしたは) or nothing (いま), so I guess ここは and get it wrong.
evidence: Answer: ここでよろしいですか, no note. Sister cards: あしたはよろしいですか, いまよろしいですか. The で I know marks a place where something is done or a means (かいぎでプレゼンをします, カードで).
fix: Add a note explaining the で in ここでよろしいですか ('will this place do?') and why it differs from あしたは and いま.

claim: The note says 'only the time word changes' between いまよろしいですか and あしたはよろしいですか, but a は appears as well, and neither note says why あした takes は and いま does not.
evidence: Back note: 'Minimal pair with あしたはよろしいですか (ashita wa yoroshii desu ka): only the time word changes.' The other card's note: 'いま (ima) becomes あしたは (ashita wa).'
fix: Say that あした picks up は (contrast: tomorrow, as opposed to today) while いま needs none.

claim: Every すき card I studied marks the liked thing with が, so I say ステーキがすきですか; this card wants は and has no note to tell me why.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Grammar & Function Words / Emma-san, do you like steak?' Answer: エマさん、ステーキはすきですか, no note. Ledger: すずきさんはスポーツがすきですか | Do you like sports, Suzuki-san?; チャンさんはワインがすきです; どんなスポーツがすきですか.
fix: Add a note saying は replaces が here to make steak the topic (as in 'as for steak, do you like it?'), or add a hint asking for steak as the topic.

claim: The note says ききます means 'ask' because a person is marked with に, but in this sentence the に on スミスさん belongs to でんわをして, not to ききます.
evidence: Target: スミスさんにでんわをして、レストランのばしょをききます. Note: 'ききます (kikimasu) here means "ask" because a person is marked with に (ni).'
fix: Say instead that ききます means 'ask' here because its object is a piece of information (ばしょ), and the person asked is the one just called.

claim: The English says 'rented', but I only learned かります as 'Borrow', so I do not think of かります for 'rent'.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'I rented a car and went for a drive. / Answering: What did you do yesterday?' Answer: くるまをかりて、ドライブをしました. Ledger: かります | Borrow; スミスさんはなかむらさんにくるまをかりました | Smith-san borrowed a car from Nakamura-san.
fix: Add to the note that かります also covers renting, or change the English to 'borrowed'.

claim: Ten other cards in this unit say 'after the X' with のあと、 and this one alone wants のあとで, with nothing on the front to choose between them.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'I'll eat after the meeting. / A coworker asks when you plan to eat supper...' Answer: かいぎのあとでたべます. Compare kaigi-no-ato-yamamoto-san 'After the meeting, I will meet Yamamoto-san.' -> かいぎのあと、やまもとさんにあいます, and smith-report-after-meeting -> かいぎのあと、レポートをかきました.
fix: Add a note saying のあと and のあとで are both correct and either answer is right, or add a hint asking for あとで.
